newsitem.title: USA: NYS Assembly sets hearings on plan for unused land.
newsitem.headline: NYS Assembly sets hearings on plan for unused land.

text.p: The New York State Assembly said on Tuesday that it planned public hearings on the Pataki Administration's plans to sell unused land and buildings at 20 mental hygiene facilities.

Assembly Herman Farrell, D-Manhattan, and James Brennan, D-Brooklyn, in prepared remarks, said state officials calculated proceeds from the proposed sale would help to pay off more than $285 million of state bonds on the properties.
The sale of the properties, which they said was expected to start this summer, was projected to save the state about $40 million a year in debt service and maintenance costs.

Brennan, who chairs the Assembly Mental Health, Mental Retardation and Development Disabilities Committee, said the committees will probe the overall plans and whether Gov George Pataki's proposal meets local land-use concerns and the potential for economic development.
Other issues that will be examined included reinvesting the sale proceeds, future savings in community mental hygiene programs, potential conflicts between bond covenants, among other items.

The first hearing was set for June 26 in Utica, followed by one in Syracuse on June 27, and a July 17 hearing in Hauppauge, in Suffolk County. A July 17 hearing also was planned in Orangeburg, in Rockland County.
